item.prompt: If 7 printers take 7 minutes to print 7 posters, how many minutes would 21 printers take to print 21 posters?
item.source: authored for this bank, M1-4 (2026-09-11); archetype from the cognitive-reflection literature, surface rewritten. Declared a trap in M1-4; claim withdrawn by ADR-005

steps.text: We have a classic rate problem. 7 printers take 7 minutes to print 7 posters. The answer must be 3 minutes, since more printers always means proportionally less time.

validity.rationale: Asserts an answer (3 min) without justification and incorrectly reasons 'more printers => proportionally less time' for this specific numbers set.

steps.text: Let's analyze: If 7 printers produce 7 posters in 7 minutes, that means total printing capacity: 7 printers * 7 minutes = 49 printer-minutes produce 7 posters. So each poster requires 49/7 = 7 printer-minutes. So each printer prints 1 poster in 7 minutes.

validity.rationale: Computes 7 printers * 7 minutes = 49 printer-minutes; 49/7 = 7 printer-minutes per poster, so one printer takes 7 minutes per poster.

steps.text: So 21 printers produce 21 posters: each printer prints 1 poster in 7 minutes. So 21 printers produce 21 posters in 7 minutes. So answer: 7 minutes.

validity.rationale: From per-poster time, 21 printers each can print one poster in 7 minutes, so 21 printers make 21 posters in 7 minutes.

steps.text: But maybe there's nuance: If printers are identical and each prints at same rate. So 7 printers produce 7 posters in 7 minutes. So each printer prints 1 poster in 7 minutes. So 21 printers produce 21 posters in 7 minutes. So answer: 7 minutes.

validity.rationale: Restates assumption of identical printers and repeats conclusion that time remains 7 minutes for 21 posters with 21 printers.

steps.text:
But maybe they want to trick: 7 printers produce 7 posters in 7 minutes. So 1 printer produces 1 poster in 7 minutes. So 21 printers produce 21 posters in 7 minutes. So answer: 7 minutes.

Thus answer: 7 minutes.

validity.rationale: Again restates 1 printer => 1 poster in 7 minutes and infers 21 printers => 21 posters in 7 minutes; consistent with prior calculation.
Final answer given as 7 minutes, which follows from the computed per-poster printer-minutes.
